_doc: Ranking weights. 'importance' is applied at build time (stored per entry, 0..1). Everything else is read by query.py at query time. Scores are additive; see README.md for the formula.

raw_type_label_suffix._doc: Label of a POI that fits no category: the value of its main OSM tag ('shop=hairdresser' -> 'Hairdresser'), plus this suffix for some keys ('office=financial' -> 'Financial office').

us_spellings._doc: The words of a type label made from OSM tag values in US spelling (the owner's answer of 2026-11-16: US spellings everywhere in the app's texts): a place's type ('neighbourhood' -> 'Neighborhood') and a POI with no category ('leisure=sports_centre' -> 'Sports center'). Applied word by word, the first letter's case kept; also to the leading type label of a place's subtitle in a pack built before ('Neighbourhood in Erie' -> 'Neighborhood in Erie'), never to names.

weights._doc: name: x tier value; importance: x entry importance (places get place_importance on top); distance: x decay; context: x context match (0..1) when the query names a place; category_hit / brand_hit: base score of a browse hit; browse_importance: x importance for browse hits; street_address: POI whose addr:street is the street in 'X on <street>'; house_located: added to a street result whose typed house number was located (an exact address), times the tier value of its name match (nothing for an any_word match: a street that only shares a word with the query) and the distance decay of the house from the anchor, and only inside the named place's municipality or county when the query names one (an exact address in town goes first; one in another town or far away does not jump a nearby street); name_when_category_or_brand: scales name matches when the whole phrase is also a category or brand word.

distance._doc: decay = 1 / (1 + d / scale_km). browse_scale_km for category and brand queries around the user (ranked mainly by distance); context_browse_scale_km when the query names a place ('gas near pittsburgh').

search._doc_browse_rtree_first: Category browse rings up to this radius walk the R*Tree box first and probe poi_cat (measured 20-100x faster at 3-30 km); larger rings let SQLite walk the category's POIs (faster at 200-500 km).
search._doc_short_prefix: 1-3 characters: places by key prefix (partial index on places), POIs from poi_prefix in the grid cells around the anchor (ring 1 = 3x3 cells of 0.1 degree, ring 2 = 5x5, ...), stopping at the first ring with short_prefix_poi_min_hits, nearest short_prefix_poi_keep kept. coverage_margin_km: a position farther than this outside the pack's bounding box is flagged out_of_coverage, and a pure category query that finds nothing there returns nothing instead of name matches.
search._doc_max_query_chars: Input cap (rule S5): the engine itself (query.py and the Kotlin engine alike) keeps only the first max_query_chars Unicode code points of the query text, before any other step; a longer text is searched as its cut.

addresses._doc: Join point to the addresses track database (data/addresses/pa-addresses.sqlite). query.py ATTACHes it read-only if it exists and looks up (street key, house number) once per distinct street key, then keeps the address point that lies in the matched street's bounding box (+ house_margin_deg). The key is street.addr_key in the search database, computed at BUILD time with the addresses track's own street_key() (abbreviated form: 'n main st'), so nothing of that track runs at query time. The engine refuses to attach when the addresses database's normalisation table version (version_table/version_key) differs from the one the search index was keyed with. Without the file, house numbers are not located.

crossing._doc: Two streets and a word between them ('state st and 12th', '&' folds to 'and', '@' reads as 'at'): where their lines (pack table street_line) come within within_m of each other. Meetings nearer than apart_m are one crossing (a divided road's two carriageways). candidates_per_side streets are asked for each side; at most max_pairs pairs whose boxes (grown by box_margin_deg) overlap are measured, and no more than max_segment_tests segment pairs in all (a pair that would go over is left out); max_results crossings are shown, before every other result, with this score.

near_street._doc: The street at a point (a dropped pin): the nearest street line within within_m, among at most max_streets streets whose box holds the point. With the addresses database: the house number of that street's address point nearest to the point, when one is within house_within_m (farther away it is somebody else's house).
